addModel.stallHelp: When the model keeps repeating the same tool call, or the same call keeps erroring, bump the request one tier higher for as long as it looks stuck. The automatic counterpart to an escalation keyword: nobody has to notice the loop and ask. Off means a stuck task keeps the model it was classified onto.
addModel.stallThresholdHelp: How many identical or failing calls count as stuck. At least 2; lower reacts sooner and misfires more.
addModel.stallWindowHelp: How far back to look, in tool calls. Never below the repeat count, since that could never be reached.
addModel.responseRawModelNameHelp: Return the resolved underlying model name in responses instead of the autorouter alias.
addModel.responseCapMaxTokens: Cap max_tokens at the tier model's output ceiling
addModel.responseCapMaxTokensHelp: Replace the caller's max_tokens with the routed tier model's output ceiling so one client value fits every tier. Off forwards the caller's value unchanged.
addModel.escalationKeywordsTooltip: Case-sensitive phrases a user can include in their message to force a bump to the next-higher complexity tier when they aren't happy with results. They can force a stronger model, but not choose which one.
addModel.escalationKeywordsHelp: Optional: when a user message contains one of these phrases, the request is bumped one tier higher than it would otherwise route to. Matching is case-sensitive, so "LITELLM ESCALATE" only fires on the exact, shouted form. Leave empty to disable.
addModel.compressionRoutingTooltip: Compression applied to the classifier's own call that picks a tier, separate from the model the request routes to.
addModel.compressionInheritPlaceholder: Inherit from the request's own compression guardrails
addModel.reminderMarkersHelp: Auto Router already ignores built-in reminder tags, such as '', when choosing a model. Leave this empty to keep the defaults. Add custom opening and closing tags to ignore the text between them when routing. Custom pairs replace the defaults, so include any built-in pairs you still need. The selected model still receives the full message. Matching is case-insensitive.
addModel.adaptiveEnableHelp: When disabled, each request always uses the model assigned to its classified tier.
addModel.adaptiveHowItWorksBody: It learns from how each conversation actually goes: does the user have to rephrase or correct the model, does it get stuck repeating itself, does it run out of tool calls, does the user seem satisfied. Combined with cost, this live feedback shifts future routing toward the models that are actually working well, and improves as more conversations come in. Until there's enough feedback, it defaults to the classified tier's model.
addModel.adaptiveQualityVsCostHelp: Higher quality weight favors more capable (pricier) models; higher cost weight favors cheaper models when the bandit has feedback to act on. Recommended: 30% quality / 70% cost split.
addModel.adaptiveEligibleAllDetail: , the router can pick across tiers, whichever fits the prompt best
addModel.adaptiveEligibleClassifiedDetail: , the router can only pick models within the classified tier
addModel.adaptiveTierDistancePenaltyHelp: Score penalty applied per tier-step away from the classified tier.
addModel.keywordTierTooltip: Match known terms and force the request straight to a chosen complexity tier, bypassing rule-based scoring.
addModel.keywordTierHelp: Optional: route requests containing specific keywords directly to a tier, e.g. route "invoice, refund, billing" to the medium tier.
addModel.keywordRequired: At least one keyword is required
addModel.semanticKeywordTooltip: Recognize related phrasing beyond exact keyword matches by comparing embeddings instead of plain text. Overrides direct keyword matching
addModel.semanticKeywordHelp: Uses same keyword-tier pairs as above and overrides direct keyword matching. Adds latency based on embedding model network request.
addModel.minMatchScoreHelp: Match only at or above this similarity score.
addModel.heuristicKeywordHelp: Each list replaces the built-in keyword list of the same name for the heuristic scorer. Leave a list empty to keep the built-in one. To add technical terms without replacing the list, use custom technical keywords under Classification Method.
addModel.scoringModeHelp: Binary uses the full weight for any hit. Match count uses half for one distinct matcher and full weight for two or more.
addModel.customDimensionMatchersHelp: Keywords match the current ask. Regex scans its first 2,048 characters and permits bounded single-character repeats up to 64. The proxy validates patterns on save.
addModel.advancedScoringHelp: Every knob below is optional. Left untouched, the router follows the shipped defaults, so it picks up any recalibration of them rather than staying pinned to the numbers shown here.
addModel.shippedDefaultsLoadFailed: Could not load the shipped defaults, so only values this router already overrides are shown. Saving still works, and an untouched knob keeps following the defaults.
addModel.groupTierBoundariesBlurb: The weighted score each tier starts at. Scores run from -1 to 1, and short or conversational prompts score below 0, so a negative boundary is a valid way to lift trivial traffic into a higher tier.
addModel.groupTokenThresholdsBlurb: Estimated prompt length, in tokens, that pushes the token count dimension to its floor or ceiling. Lengths between the two score neutral.
addModel.groupDimensionWeightsBlurb: Changing a weight rebalances the other built-in and custom weights to total 1.00. Save stores those values. Untouched routers keep their existing weights.
addModel.warnDecreasingBoundaries: These boundaries decrease, so every tier between them is unreachable and its traffic routes elsewhere.
addModel.warnShortNotBelowLong: The short threshold is not below the long one, so no prompt length scores neutral on length.
addModel.reasoningOverrideHelp: Two or more reasoning markers promote a request to the reasoning tier, but only once its weighted score reaches this floor.
addModel.reasoningOverrideTracksUnset: Left untouched, it tracks the Simple to Medium boundary.
addModel.reasoningOverrideTracksSet: Left untouched, it tracks the Simple to Medium boundary, currently {floor}.
addModel.reasoningOverrideSetZero: Set it to 0 to promote on the markers alone.
addModel.rebalanceNeedDefaults: Load the shipped defaults before changing weights
addModel.rebalanceInvalidStored: Existing weights must be finite and nonnegative; custom weights must be greater than 0 and at most 1
addModel.rebalanceDimensionGone: The dimension is no longer available
addModel.rebalanceWeightRange: Use a weight from 0 to 1; custom dimensions must stay greater than 0
addModel.rebalanceTooLarge: Existing weights are too large to rebalance
addModel.rebalanceNoShare: Leave a positive share for every custom dimension, or remove it first
addModel.scoringDefaultExplanation: The router scores each request across 7 built-in dimensions: token count, code presence, reasoning markers, technical terms, simple indicators, multi-step patterns, and question complexity, plus any custom dimensions you add. The weighted score determines the tier:
addModel.scoringHeuristicV2Explanation: The router estimates success probability for all four tiers with its calibrated model, then selects the first tier that meets the success threshold. If none qualify, it selects Reasoning. It runs locally with no classifier API call.
addModel.scoringCustomPromptHeuristicFallback: This router classifies with your own prompt, so the tier comes from whatever rubric it states. The four tier names stay fixed. The scoring below is the heuristic, which now runs only when the classifier call fails:
addModel.scoringCustomPromptDefaultModelFallback: This router classifies with your own prompt, so the tier comes from whatever rubric it states. The four tier names stay fixed. The scoring below no longer runs at all, since a failed classifier routes to the default model instead:
addModel.scoreAboveWithMarkers: Score > {boundary} (or 2+ reasoning markers with a score of at least {floor})
addModel.tierRangesUnavailable: The tier score ranges could not be loaded from the proxy.
addModel.inactiveHeuristicV2Help: Only used when Heuristic v2 is selected
addModel.successThresholdHelp: Minimum predicted success probability, from 0 to 1. Higher values favor more capable tiers. Leave blank to use the artifact default
addModel.decideLocallyHelp: A request the scorer places at or below this tier routes there without a classifier call. Anything the scorer places higher, and anything it found no signal for at all, goes to the classifier instead
addModel.boundaryMarginHelp: A score further than this from every tier boundary routes on the scorer's own tier, however expensive that tier is. A score closer than this, and anything the scorer found no signal for at all, goes to the classifier to break the tie
addModel.timeoutHelp: How long the classifier call has before it fails and the fallback below takes over.
addModel.classifierPromptTooltip: Every rubric uses the same four tiers. They differ in the worked examples that show the classifier where the boundary between tiers sits, and the Business rubric also rewrites the tier definitions for business traffic. Pick the rubric, and write your own opening instructions and calibration examples, inside the prompt editor.

addModel.contextWindowSizeHelp: Number of prior user turns sent to the classifier provider, excluding tool output and harness reminders. LLM and decision model classifiers default to 3 turns. Set to 0 to omit conversation history. The current message and selected system text are still sent.
addModel.contextBudgetHelp: Total characters of prior conversation sent to the classifier. Turns are taken newest first and quoted whole while they fit, so a short conversation is never cut.

addModel.includeAssistantTurnsTooltip: Off by default. Enabling it changes tier decisions, and therefore spend, for an existing router, and sends assistant text to the classifier model, which may be a different provider than the routed model.
addModel.includeAssistantTurnsHelp: Let the classifier read the assistant's replies, so difficulty the model stated rather than the user stays visible: a plan the assistant calls complex, approved with "yes", is classified on the work being approved. Context Window Size then counts the last N turns across both roles rather than the last N user turns.
addModel.customTechnicalKeywordsTooltip: Domain-specific terms appended to the built-in technical keyword list. Prompts containing these terms score higher on the technical dimension and route to more capable models.

tiles.totalInfo: The sum of recorded savings in the three tiles beside it. Auto-router requests without an estimate are excluded. Its caching term is the LiteLLM-injected share; caching supplied by clients or providers appears only in the caching tile. Total figure.
tiles.compressionInfo: Tokens Headroom removed before the call, priced at the model.s input rate.
tiles.cachingInfo: What caching saved against paying the input rate for every token: the discount on tokens served from cache, less the premium providers charge to write a cache entry. The headline figure is the share LiteLLM earned by inserting the breakpoints itself, through configured injection points or auto prompt caching. The total beside it also counts requests that arrived with their own cache_control and providers that cache implicitly. Either can be negative on traffic that writes more cache than it reuses, which is why the headline is not always the smaller of the two.
tiles.autoInfo: Sum of available per-request savings estimates against each router.s highest-tier baseline, net of classifier cost. Requests without an estimate contribute nothing to this subtotal; this does not mean they saved zero. Historical records retain the estimator used when they were written.
